claude.sample_unit: composite LLM-generated texts (4 models × 3 literacy tiers; 72 outputs aggregated)

links.outcome: Readability (FKGL) of LLM osteoporosis materials for low-literacy prompts against target of grade 8 or below
links.effect: Low-literacy tier: DeepSeek-V3.1 FKGL 3.99, ChatGPT-5 5.71, DeepSeek-R2 5.81 met FKGL ≤ 8; ChatGPT-4o did not (10.37). Moderate tier: only DeepSeek-V3.1 met target (6.17).
links.quote: Three models met the pre‑specified readability target (FKGL ≤ 8): DeepSeek‑V3.1 (FKGL 3.99), ChatGPT‑5 (FKGL 5.71), and DeepSeek‑R2 (FKGL 5.81). ChatGPT‑4o did not meet the target (FKGL 10.37).

links.outcome: Plain-language readability of AI-generated patient education across literacy tiers
links.effect: Three of four models met FKGL ≤ 8 for low literacy; ChatGPT-4o produced FKGL 10.37 for low tier; moderate-tier texts of three models were about 9th grade (FKGL 9.01–9.23).
links.quote: The remaining three models produced texts at approximately 9th grade level (FKGL range 9.01–9.23).

links.outcome: Content accuracy and quality of LLM outputs for low versus high health literacy prompts
links.effect: Content accuracy lowest for low-literacy outputs (mean 12.54/18, 69.7%) vs high-literacy (14.10/18, 78.3%); DISCERN totals lowest for low-literacy variants (36–39/80).
links.quote: High‐literacy outputs demonstrated the highest content accuracy (mean 14.10/18, 78.3%), followed by moderate‐literacy outputs (mean 13.44/18, 74.7%) and low‐literacy outputs (mean 12.54/18, 69.7%).

links.outcome: Presence of sources/references and publication dates in LLM-generated patient education
links.effect: All 12 composite texts (100%) scored ≤2/5 on DISCERN Q4 (sources) and Q5 (dates); all outputs lacked citations.
links.quote: Q4 (sources/references, 100%), Q5 (publication/update date, 100%), Q7 (additional resources, 92%), Q8 (uncertainty statements, 83%), Q10 (risks of treatment, 75%), and Q12 (consequences of non‐treatment, 75%).

links.outcome: Explicit uncertainty statements in LLM-generated patient education (DISCERN Q8)
links.effect: 10 of 12 texts (83%) scored ≤2/5 on uncertainty statements; no model achieved acceptable performance on Q8.
links.quote: No model achieved acceptable performance on Q4, Q5, Q7, or Q8.

links.outcome: Guideline concordance and completeness of LLM osteoporosis content versus NOF/IOF guidelines
links.effect: Mean accuracy 13.24/18 (73.7%); no hallucinations detected; inaccuracies mostly omissions, lowest in pharmacotherapy (2.04/3) and screening (2.11/3).
links.quote: No output received a score of 0 in any domain, and no hallucinations (i.e., factually incorrect statements contrary to established guidelines) were detected in any output.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of outputs across repeated runs on a subset of prompts
links.effect: Rerun of 10% of prompts (n=7) showed high consistency; minor wording variation, mean absolute FKGL difference < 0.3, no effect on DISCERN scores.
links.quote: The generated outputs showed high consistency in factual content and structure, with only minor wording variations that did not affect DISCERN scores or readability metrics (mean absolute difference in FKGL < 0.3).

links.outcome: blinded clinician scoring reliability
links.effect: DISCERN total-score ICC was 0.87 (95% CI: 0.76–0.94), indicating good to excellent reliability.
links.quote: The ICC for DISCERN total scores was 0.87 (95% CI: 0.76–0.94), indicating good to excellent reliability.

links.outcome: repeated-run output variability
links.effect: Repeated 10% subset (n = 7 prompts): high factual/structural consistency; minor wording variation; mean absolute FKGL difference < 0.3.
links.quote: The generated outputs showed high consistency in factual content and structure, with only minor wording variations that did not affect DISCERN scores or readability metrics (mean absolute difference in FKGL < 0.3).

links.outcome: readability grade level for low-literacy materials
links.effect: Low tier: DeepSeek-V3.1 3.99, ChatGPT-5 5.71, DeepSeek-R2 5.81 met FKGL≤8; ChatGPT-4o 10.37 did not.
links.quote: ChatGPT‑4o did not meet the target (FKGL 10.37).

links.outcome: content accuracy by health-literacy tier
links.effect: Content accuracy decreased by tier: high 14.10/18 (78.3%), moderate 13.44/18 (74.7%), low 12.54/18 (69.7%).
links.quote: High‐literacy outputs demonstrated the highest content accuracy (mean 14.10/18, 78.3%), followed by moderate‐literacy outputs (mean 13.44/18, 74.7%) and low‐literacy outputs (mean 12.54/18, 69.7%).

links.outcome: supporting citations and update metadata
links.effect: Q4 sources/references and Q5 publication/update date: 12/12 (100%) low; all outputs lacked citations and dates.
links.quote: All outputs lacked citations, publication dates, quantitative risk data, and uncertainty statements.

links.outcome: uncertainty statements in generated education
links.effect: Q8 uncertainty statements: 10/12 (83%) outputs scored ≤2/5.
links.quote: Six items showed low scores in ≥ 75% of outputs: Q4 (sources/references, 100%), Q5 (publication/update date, 100%), Q7 (additional resources, 92%), Q8 (uncertainty statements, 83%), Q10 (risks of treatment, 75%), and Q12 (consequences of non‐treatment, 75%).

links.outcome: guideline completeness for osteoporosis content
links.effect: Pharmacotherapy 2.04/3 and screening 2.11/3 were lowest; low-literacy outputs omitted medication names or DXA thresholds.
links.quote: The highest accuracy scores were observed in the risk factors domain (mean 2.45/3) and prevention domain (mean 2.38/3), while the lowest were observed in pharmacotherapy (mean 2.04/3) and screening (mean 2.11/3), where low‐literacy outputs often omitted specific medication names or DXA screening thresholds.

links.outcome: Readability target attainment for low health literacy
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o failed the low-literacy readability target (FKGL 10.37), whereas DeepSeek-V3.1 (3.99), ChatGPT-5 (5.71), and DeepSeek-R2 (5.81) met the FKGL <= 8 target
links.quote: ChatGPT‑4o did not meet the target (FKGL 10.37).

links.outcome: Guideline content accuracy across literacy tiers
links.effect: Mean content accuracy was 14.10/18 (78.3%) for high-literacy, 13.44/18 (74.7%) for moderate-literacy, and 12.54/18 (69.7%) for low-literacy outputs
links.quote: High‑literacy outputs demonstrated the highest content accuracy (mean 14.10/18, 78.3%), followed by moderate‑literacy outputs (mean 13.44/18, 74.7%) and low‑literacy outputs (mean 12.54/18, 69.7%).
